outcome.technical: FIXES (a)-(h). (a) _status_facts.phase_timing(summaries, statuses) sums only DONE tasks with a window. Every other task carrying a record goes in a new aggregate key leftOut {id: cancelled | not finished | no window}, so withoutWindow is kept and no key is lost. timing_rollup passes the statuses. PHASE_TIMING_BASIS says done tasks. statuses is now a required argument: a default would silently leave every task out as not finished. (b) _task_timing.summarize names a stages value that is not a list under missing as timing.stages (STAGES_FIELD) and gives no window or figures. A stage failing stage_problems was already named as timing.stages[i]. A new is_unreadable(summary) tells those two apart from a readable record that has no window. audit-status _time_cell prints not readable for them and never prints a window figure. (c) The gate sentence now reads: --gate reads no timing figure, only the validator's verdict on the record, so a malformed record can trip the default invalid condition. It is in PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, CHANGELOG.md and COMPATIBILITY.md. git grep for the old claim (reads none of it) finds no other hit. tc11 is retitled, and tc13 proves a kind of lunch trips --gate (exit 1, invalid). (d) The no window value (no first start, or a completion before it) and not readable are documented in status.md, PBG, CHANGELOG and the _time_cell docstring. tc14 renders both values, and tc16 renders the overrun clause. (e) The reopen rule (the first start never moves, so the closed time sits inside the window as unattributed time) is stated in the _task_timing module and summarize docstrings, the schema's firstStartedAt description, PBG, status.md and CHANGELOG. (f) The schema gains $defs/timingStamp. Its pattern is _usage_core._TS_RE, plus a refusal of year 0000 and of months outside 01-12, which parse_ts also refuses (probe: parse_ts gives None for 0000-01-01, 2026-00-01, 2026-13-01 and a lowercase t, and accepts day 00 and hour 99, which the pattern also accepts). firstStartedAt and stage startedAt $ref it. basis gains a non-blank pattern, and runId gains minLength 1 and the same pattern. DEVIATION on ms 1.0: no JSON Schema can refuse it, because draft 2020-12 integer admits integral floats and JSON gives 1.0 and 1 one value (ajv reads both as 1, and the repo's _json_schema says the same). So I aligned the other side: stage_problems admits an integral float for ms and round (_is_whole), and _by_kind sums int(ms). Now a plan the schema passes is one the plugin passes, and 1.5 is refused by both (tt22). Acceptance (6)'s 'refused' therefore holds for three of the four loosenesses, and the fourth is closed by agreement. (g) audit-status._wall_duration prints a h mm m past an hour and a d hh h past a day, in the time column and the phase line only. _fmt.human_duration is untouched, and tc19 pins 1840 m 00 s for its other callers. (h) tt2 now compares against figures written in the case. tt7 compares the basis to a literal. tt10 is retitled to what it checks, with a comment naming tc1 and tc2 as the byte-for-byte cases. tc6 compares the whole clause with endswith, so order counts. tmd3 recomputes the window through datetime and the attributed share from the stage lengths, instead of using the identity. tmd4 validates every generated record against the schema's timing definition. Also: audit-status imports _task_timing, and the derived import line in PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md:438 was updated (test__deps green).
